relations.subject: search:index-name-uniqueness
relations.evidence: For indexes created with Couchbase Server version 7.6 and later, index names must be unique inside a bucket and scope. You cannot have 2 indexes with the same name inside the same bucket and scope on a Capella operational cluster running version 7.6 or later.

notable_absence.finding: This page states no privilege, role, or credential-type requirement at all for creating a Search index - it has no Prerequisites section whatsoever. This matches the finding already logged for its server/ counterpart (server/search/create-search-indexes.json), which flagged the identical gap for the RBAC 'Search Admin' role. It also contrasts with sibling cloud/vector-index/ pages in this same batch (composite-vector-index.md, hyperscale-vector-index.md), which explicitly document requiresCapellaRole gates (Organization Owner / Project Owner / Data Writer) for index creation - see this batch's cross_product_finding on that topic.

cross_product_finding: Two separate findings. (1) This Capella page cites two distinct literal 'Couchbase Server version X.Y' markers (8.0 for synonym source and scoring model configuration; 7.6 for index name uniqueness), continuing the recurring pattern already flagged in cloud/search/search-index-params.json and cloud/vector-index/use-vector-indexes.json of Capella search/ documentation gating features on the underlying managed-cluster's Couchbase Server version rather than a Capella-native availability concept. (2) None of the three Capella search/ pages in this batch (this page, create-search-index-ui.json, create-search-index-alias.json) document any RBAC role or privilege requirement for creating Search indexes or aliases - a gap that becomes more notable when contrasted with this same batch's cloud/vector-index/ pages, which DO explicitly require one of three Capella management-plane roles (requiresCapellaRole) to create a vector index. Either Capella's Search Service genuinely has no comparable access-control gate (a real product difference), or the requirement is simply undocumented on these particular pages - flagging for the coordinator since this spans multiple pages/components, not just one.
